note: Skills any office uses from any client: the AI-tells guide (facts and word lists a placement skill applies), and two for a GitHub repository through GitHub's own MCP server (code-change opens a pull request; actions-check looks at the runs). Same shape as AI4RA/prompt-library's component_catalog.json, hand-maintained. No component names a client.

components.name: ai-tells-guide
components.summary: The reference material for editing prose so it no longer reads like machine output: twenty-nine families of tells (words, sentences, structure, formatting, residue) with their word lists, the invariants an edit keeps, and what a report of the edit contains. Facts and reference only; the order of work is the placement skill's.

components.name: code-change
components.summary: Make a described change to a GitHub repository as a pull request: read the files first, commit the whole changed files to a new agent/<login>/<slug> branch, open a pull request against the default branch, start the checks (or a named workflow) and report the links. Never writes to main, never merges, never waits for checks, never commits a secret; the person reviews and merges.
triggers: make this change in the repo

components.name: actions-check
components.summary: One look at a repository's GitHub Actions: the latest runs on a branch, pull request or workflow with status, conclusion and links, and for each failure the job, the step and the first real error from the failed jobs' logs. A snapshot, never a wait; reruns or cancellations only when asked by name.
